description: Test-only declarative transition/state descriptor for veles-v1.md section 11 (pairing, client pairing, session, authorization classes) plus the durable trust-record machines of section 5 (OTP2-STA-010/010a/010b/010c). Every transition mirrors a normative table row or requirement; effects are the Effect/Timeout/Failure columns. The normative document governs; a disagreement between this descriptor and veles-v1.md is a defect that fails the checks. Numeric ceilings are never duplicated here: guards reference limits.json names, resolved by checks/state.mjs. Simulated crypto outcomes (tag_ok, hmac_ok, sig_ok, act_mac_ok, peer_state) are trace inputs (OTP2-FIX-004), never conformance evidence. record_type_directions = originating direction of each record type (OTP2-ENC-020, 0x01 client->phone, 0x02 phone->client). record_effects = orientation-neutral effect names appended for accepted session records. record_flow = per-record pull/push outstanding counter bookkeeping (0x0204 settles outstanding push only on known events; unknown ack is a semantic no-op). record_state_machinesrecord_flags = OTP2-REC-031 canonical response_to_pull correlation is carried in the flags byte (bit3) and modeled in traces via the simulate flag pull_response; record_effects may carry {always, on_flag} and record_flow may carry dec_if_flag for the conditional settle. One-use code: phone pairing encodes OTP2-CRY-009a (code consumed at successful cB verification); post-code connection loss resumes via signed recovery ONLY where usable persisted peer records exist on both endpoints (an interruption before the peer identity was persisted leaves no usable record: repair via a fresh explicit pairing window; OTP2-CRY-009a). Prepare gates encode OTP2-STA-010a (original enrollment) and 010b step 0 (recovery prepare under OTP2-CRY-019f keys). Session class selection encodes OTP2-SID-001 with the client upgrade-before-selection rule. binds each trace role to its local durable-record machine for class determination (OTP2-SID-001).

frame_directions.description: Pre-auth plaintext frame payload directions (OTP2-ENC-010): direction byte 0x01 = client->phone, 0x02 = phone->client. Frames arrive at the endpoint whose inbound direction matches; arrival at the opposite endpoint is a role/context mismatch.

enrollment_types.description: OTP2-CRY-020a: record types allowed on the original enrollment connection.

on_flag.description: OTP2-REC-031 canonical response_to_pull correlation (flags bit3): set only when this record answers one pull_request; a stale flag report with no outstanding pull is accepted, never underflows the counter, and settles nothing beyond a legitimate outstanding pull.

dec_if_flag.description: flags bit3 response_to_pull: settle exactly one outstanding pull; absent/clear flag (unsolicited notice) never settles; no underflow when nothing is outstanding (stale report).

public_persisted_fields.description: OTP2-CRY-019g: only these fields may appear as persisted-state keys (besides machine:peer overrides). Any other key - in particular any secret - is a trust-boundary violation.

on_direction_mismatch.description: A frame arriving in the phone's own outbound direction is a role/context mismatch: generic pre-auth failure, and while a pairing execution is in flight the current connection is disconnected (ephemeral execution state erased; the pairing window, attempt budget and rate accounting persist; a next attempt requires a fresh connection).

trans.description: OTP2-CRY-009a: verifying cB consumes the code — the pairing window closes for this pairing_id and the code is erased. Later continuation is CONDITIONAL on usable persisted peer records: once the peer's identity record was authenticated and the durable pending record exists, a disconnect resumes via signed recovery (OTP2-STA-010b) — never a second code entry; if the interruption lands BEFORE the peer's identity was persisted (no usable peer record), recovery does not exist and the only path is an explicitly user-opened NEW pairing window (fresh pairing_id, fresh code) after the one-sided record is cancelled/revoked/expired (OTP2-STA-012).

OTP2-STA-010a (atomic usable-record persistence): the phone derives `ET` from the canonical identity bodies — its own is locally known; the client's once authenticated — and ATOMICALLY persists the COMPLETE `pending` record INCLUDING `ET` (public fields only), entering `awaiting_commit` and releasing `enrollment_prepare` ONLY after durable persistence success. A persistence failure or crash before completion publishes nothing (no prepare is sent) and leaves no usable record (repair via a fresh explicit pairing window; OTP2-CRY-009a).

R1 persistence boundary: the durable persist failed/crashed before completion — nothing usable is or may be published: no `enrollment_prepare` is sent, no pending record exists (durable deleted); repair via a fresh explicit pairing window (OTP2-CRY-009a).

OTP2-CRY-009a: after the code is consumed and the closed window, the enrollment connection cannot resume by re-entering the code. A usable persisted peer record exists here by construction (pending/committed_waiting_ack), so continuation on a NEW connection is signed recovery (OTP2-STA-010b); the record persists (OTP2-STA-012 refuses a second enrollment while held).

Post-code states (the durable record is pending/committed_waiting_ack by construction): the window is closed, so the 30 s inactivity timeout drops the enrollment connection to idle; continuation happens via signed recovery (OTP2-STA-010b), which exists exactly because the persisted peer record exists.

OTP2-CRY-009a: after the code is consumed and the closed window, the enrollment connection cannot resume by re-entering the code. A usable persisted peer record exists here by construction (pending/committed_waiting_ack), so continuation on a NEW connection is signed recovery (OTP2-STA-010b); the record persists (OTP2-STA-012 refuses a second enrollment while held).

Post-code states (the durable record is pending/committed_waiting_ack by construction): the window is closed, so the 30 s inactivity timeout drops the enrollment connection to idle; continuation happens via signed recovery (OTP2-STA-010b), which exists exactly because the persisted peer record exists.
Defensive row: enrollment_protected with a persisted record exists only if the client identity was authenticated and the machine ordering changed; recovery of OTP2-STA-010b exists.

R1 (reviewer subagent): the interruption came before the client identity record was authenticated/persisted — NO usable peer record exists; the code stays consumed (OTP2-CRY-009a) and recovery does not exist. The pairing continuation is repair-only: an explicitly user-opened NEW pairing window (fresh pairing_id, fresh code) re-enrolls the same installation (OTP2-STA-012 governs a still-held one-sided record).

R1: cancelling with no in-flight pairing execution only clears ephemeral remnants on this machine; the durable one-sided record removal is the durable record machine's own cancel/revocation/expiry path (OTP2-CRY-009a).

Defensive row (record exists only after the client identity was authenticated; see connection_lost split): the inactivity timeout drops the enrollment connection; continuation via signed recovery only (OTP2-STA-010b).

R1 residual: no usable persisted peer record — the timeout drops the connection; signed recovery does not exist and the only path is an explicitly user-opened NEW pairing window (fresh pairing_id, fresh code; the consumed code is never reused) after the one-sided record is cancelled/revoked/expired (OTP2-STA-012).

on_direction_mismatch.description: A frame arriving in the client's own outbound direction is a role/context mismatch: visible generic failure; while pairing is in flight the current connection is disconnected.

trans.description: OTP2-STA-010a (atomic usable-record persistence): the client derives `ET` from the canonical identity bodies — the phone's once authenticated + its own locally known — and ATOMICALLY persists the COMPLETE `pending` record INCLUDING `ET` (public fields only); its own identity record is released ONLY after durable persistence success. A persistence failure or crash before completion publishes nothing (no identity is sent) and leaves no usable record (repair via a fresh explicit pairing window; OTP2-CRY-009a).

R1 persistence boundary: the durable persist failed/crashed before completion — the client's identity is NOT released, nothing usable is published, and no pending record exists (durable deleted); the endpoint requires the no-usable-record cleanup/fresh-window path (OTP2-CRY-009a).

OTP2-STA-010a prepare gate: the client's commit is authorized only by verifying the enrollment_prepare MAC (stage 0x00) of the CURRENT enrollment connection. verified_prepare_ready is the prepare-verified state; no commit is ever sent from awaiting_prepare.
Early-prepare guard: an enrollment_prepare arriving before the client released its own identity record is an ordering violation (the phone cannot legitimately have produced it yet).
OTP2-STA-010a: a lost prepare means this client sends NO commit on this connection; its durable pending record persists and continuation goes through recovery (OTP2-STA-010b).

R1: cancelling with no in-flight pairing execution only clears ephemeral remnants on this machine; the durable one-sided record removal is the durable record machine's own cancel/revocation/expiry path (OTP2-CRY-009a).
OTP2-SID-001: phone record active → peer_state 0x01.
OTP2-SID-001: phone record below active → peer_state 0x02.
OTP2-SID-001: client outbound peer_state 0x01 while its record is in the active family — including the incomplete active_activation_pending mirror.
OTP2-SID-001: client record pending reports peer_state 0x02 (below active).

OTP2-SID-001 / OTP2-STA-010c: the signed+encrypted phone-active proof upgrades the incomplete active_activation_pending mirror to fully-active BEFORE class selection; both endpoints fix the class full on this first valid post-pairing reconnect. The client's outbound confirmation byte in this state is 0x01 (active family).
OTP2-STA-010b step 5: phone still below active — no upgrade; recovery class, the client re-sends the activation_ack.
Defensively exact: a client record still pending is always recovery-only; the client re-commits after this session's verified prepare (OTP2-STA-010b step 0/1).
OTP2-SID-001: a phone record below active is always activation_recovery on both its own side and (by the client matrix) for a pending client; committed_waiting_ack re-ack per step 5.
OTP2-STA-010b step 0 (client view): the phone's recovery prepare (stage 0x00 under K_rec_phone) re-attests the durable ET; prepare_verified gates this session's commit.

OTP2-STA-010a/010b step 1: a recovery commit is sent ONLY after this session's verified enrollment_prepare (the fresh-ET proof bound to the signed handshake), and only while the local client record is pending.

OTP2-STA-010b step 0 (exact peer rule): whenever the CLIENT's confirmation reported peer_state 0x02 (the client is below active-confirmed) — whether the phone's own record is pending or committed_waiting_ack, and on full_pending_peer sessions — the phone sends the recovery prepare (recovery MAC, stage 0x00 under K_rec_phone, bound to the persisted ET) BEFORE the client's commit. When the client reported 0x01 no prepare is sent: the client is beyond commit and re-sends the ack (step 5), or the session is full.
OTP2-REC-031: the blocked policy response (flags bit3 response_to_pull set) answers exactly one outstanding pull_request; the client settles on it.
OTP2-REC-031: an unsolicited policy observation (bit3 clear) — at full-session start or when the observed policy changes before an eligible delivery; it NEVER settles a pull.
A process load (or restart) with no session slot present leaves the slot absent; durable trust is unaffected here — the record machines own restart semantics.

on_direction_mismatch.description: A Veles pre-auth frame arriving on a session-machine connection in the endpoint's own outbound direction is rejected, never ignored; on an open session it tears the session down.

trans.description: OTP2-REC-035 full_pending_peer reachability note: a late/duplicate commit against an already-active record is an idempotent statement duplicate — NO state regression (committed state is never re-entered); the phone re-sends activation_complete so a still-pending peer can complete.

R1: a same-installation re-enrollment after the earlier one-sided/inactive record was genuinely deleted (explicit cancel/revocation or expiry, OTP2-CRY-009a) creates a fresh pending record; while any record is HELD the duplicate guard (OTP2-STA-012) refuses it.
R1 persistence boundary: a persist failure/crash before completion leaves NO usable record — the durable machine records the cleanup (deleted), and nothing usable exists to publish.

OTP2-CRY-019a: an activation MAC that does not verify rejects the activation sequence (generic failure, erase the incomplete state, no partial access) — mirrors the phone's commit/ack MAC-failure erasure.
